citations.narrative:
A primary enclosure housing 8 geese and another primary enclosure housing 6 geese both did not contain a pool or other
aquatic area. Failure to provide an aquatic area prevents these birds from exhibiting certain normal, species behaviors
and can lead to poor condition, debility, stress, and abnormal behavioral patterns. Primary enclosures housing wading
and aquatic birds must contain a pool or other aquatic areas (e.g., ponds, waterfalls, fountains, and other water features)
and a dry area that allows easy ingress or egress of the pool or other aquatic area. Pools and other aquatic areas must be
of sufficient surface area and depth to allow each bird to make normal postural and social adjustments, such as
immersion, bathing or swimming with adequate freedom of movement and freedom to escape from aggression
demonstrated by other birds in the enclosure.
Correct by 10/21/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:

U.S. Department of Agriculture

Mailstop #3W11
